source.title: Understanding generalization error of SGD in nonconvex optimization
source.authors: Yi Zhou; Ying-Bin Liang; Hui-Shuai Zhang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The experiments vary the fraction of random labels and report that the neural networks reach a stated training-error threshold; they do not reproduce the original study's full set of measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that neural-network training was stopped once training error fell below 0.2% for all random-label settings. Figure 1 reports on-average gradient variance, not training or test error; its plotted values are figure-only and are not extracted as rows because they do not measure the behaviors named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The neural-network experiments use SGD and report training error below 0.2% at every tested label-corruption probability, including fully random labels. This directly tests the fitting component of V1 and V4, although the main experimental outcome is gradient variance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the random-label experiment: gradient variance increases with corruption, which the authors interpret as consistent with previously observed generalization degradation. Their broader conclusion also concerns improved probabilistic generalization bounds and stronger concentration guarantees with strongly convex regularizers. They do not independently report a test-error trajectory across label-corruption levels.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies random-label probability in three experiments and measures on-average gradient variance; it does not reproduce the original study's training and test error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that on-average gradient variance increases with the fraction of random labels across the experiments. The neural-network training endpoint is a shared below-0.2% error threshold for all settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On-average stochastic-gradient variance increases with label-replacement probability in all three Figure 1 experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing random-label corruption increases late-training stochastic-gradient variance.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 reports smaller generalization gaps and worse training performance as the strongly convex regularization weight increases; random-label conditions are not specified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stronger regularization can reduce the generalization gap while worsening training performance.

record.problems: The paper does not report test error for its own experiments. Neural-network training error is described as a stopping condition shared across settings rather than separate outcome values. Figure 1's plotted variance values are figure-only in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 reports on-average gradient variance by random-label probability for logistic regression on a9a, a three-layer ReLU network on MNIST, and Resnet-18 on CIFAR10. These values do not measure any version's named behavior. Logistic regression is not a deep network.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error and explicit verification that architecture and training hyperparameters remained unchanged across label conditions.
Relative training time and convergence slowdown as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Steadily increasing test error toward chance and preservation of the remaining generalizable signal. Gradient variance does not measure these outcomes.
Whether regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing regularization preserves good true-label generalization.
The temporal order of learning real patterns and memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text identifies itself as arXiv:1802.06903v3 (2019); its correspondence to the supplied DOI cannot be verified here. The shared stopping statement supports near-zero fitting but supplies neither exact per-condition errors nor uncertainty. Figure 1's horizontal axes do not establish comparative total training times.

versions.untested_parts: Test error at chance and whether architecture and training hyperparameters were unchanged.
